question: How far can the danger zone extend from the front bumper of a school bus?
choice_a: As much as 30 feet, with the first 10 feet being the most dangerous
choice_b: 50 feet in every direction
choice_c: Exactly 5 feet
choice_d: Only the width of the bus itself
explanation: The danger zone may extend as much as 30 feet from the front bumper, with the first 10 feet being the most dangerous; it also extends 10 feet from each side and 10 feet behind the rear bumper.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 10 - School Buses, p. 10-1

question: Why is the area to the left of a school bus always considered dangerous?
choice_a: Because the exhaust pipe is located there
choice_b: Because the fuel tank is located there
choice_c: Because it is a blind spot for the driver at all times
choice_d: Because of passing cars
explanation: The area to the left of the bus is always considered dangerous because of passing cars.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 10 - School Buses, p. 10-1

question: The outside left and right side flat mirrors should be adjusted so the driver can see what, among other things?
choice_a: Only oncoming traffic in the opposite lane
choice_b: The inside of the bus only
choice_c: 200 feet or 4 bus lengths behind the bus
choice_d: Only the front bumper
explanation: The flat mirrors should be adjusted so the driver can see 200 feet or 4 bus lengths behind the bus, along the sides of the bus, and the rear tires touching the ground.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 10 - School Buses, p. 10-1

question: How far can the blind spot directly behind a school bus extend?
choice_a: Up to 400 feet, depending on the length and width of the bus
choice_b: It never extends beyond the rear bumper
choice_c: Exactly 100 feet in all cases
choice_d: No more than 20 feet
explanation: The blind spot behind the bus extends 50 to 150 feet and could extend up to 400 feet depending on the length and width of the bus.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 10 - School Buses, p. 10-1

question: What should the outside left and right side convex mirrors be positioned to show?
choice_a: Only the rear license plate
choice_b: The entire side of the bus up to the mirror mounts, front of the rear tires, and at least one traffic lane on either side
choice_c: Only the sky above the bus for weather awareness
choice_d: Only the interior aisle of the bus
explanation: The convex mirrors should be positioned to see the entire side of the bus up to the mirror mounts, the front of the rear tires touching the ground, and at least one traffic lane on either side of the bus.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 10 - School Buses, p. 10-2

question: What is the purpose of the outside left and right side crossover mirrors?
choice_a: To check tire pressure without leaving the driver's seat
choice_b: To see behind a trailer being towed
choice_c: To see the front bumper danger zone directly in front of the bus that is not visible by direct vision
choice_d: To monitor the engine compartment temperature
explanation: Crossover mirrors are used to see the front bumper 'danger zone' area directly in front of the bus that is not visible by direct vision, and to view the danger zone to the sides.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 10 - School Buses, p. 10-2

question: What is the overhead inside rearview mirror on a school bus used for?
choice_a: To check for tailgating vehicles only
choice_b: To monitor passenger activity inside the bus
choice_c: To check the condition of the rear tires
choice_d: To view the fuel gauge reflection
explanation: The overhead inside rearview mirror is mounted above the windshield on the driver's side and is used to monitor passenger activity inside the bus.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 10 - School Buses, p. 10-2

question: According to the manual, when are more students killed than as passengers inside a school bus?
choice_a: While seated during normal travel
choice_b: While getting on or off the school bus
choice_c: While the bus is parked at the school overnight
choice_d: While riding on a school activity trip on the freeway
explanation: The manual states 'More students are killed while getting on or off a school bus each year than are killed as passengers inside of a school bus.'
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 10 - School Buses, p. 10-2

question: When should a driver turn on the right turn signal before pulling over for a school bus stop?
choice_a: Immediately upon spotting students, regardless of distance
choice_b: One mile before the stop
choice_c: Only after coming to a complete stop
choice_d: About 100-300 feet, or approximately 3-5 seconds, before pulling over
explanation: The driver should turn on the right turn signal indicator about 100-300 feet or approximately 3-5 seconds before pulling over.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 10 - School Buses, p. 10-3

question: When stopping, how far away from students should the front bumper of the school bus be?
choice_a: Right at the edge of the group of students
choice_b: At least 50 feet away
choice_c: There is no set distance
choice_d: At least 10 feet away from students at the designated stop
explanation: Bring the school bus to a full stop with the front bumper at least 10 feet away from students at the designated stop, forcing students to walk to the bus so the driver has a better view of their movements.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 10 - School Buses, p. 10-3

question: What should the driver do with the transmission and parking brake at each stop?
choice_a: Place the transmission in Neutral and set the parking brake
choice_b: Leave the transmission in Drive with foot on the brake
choice_c: Turn off the engine and remove the key at every stop
choice_d: Shift into Reverse to discourage students from crossing behind
explanation: When stopping, place the transmission in Neutral and set the parking brake at each stop.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 10 - School Buses, p. 10-3

question: During loading, when should students board the bus?
choice_a: Only when signaled by the driver
choice_b: Only after the driver has turned off the engine
choice_c: Whenever they see the door open
choice_d: As soon as the bus stops moving
explanation: Students should board the bus only when signaled by the driver, boarding slowly, in single file, and using the handrail.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 10 - School Buses, p. 10-4

question: When a student must cross the roadway in front of the bus, how far should they first walk from the side of the bus?
choice_a: Only to the edge of the bus's front bumper
choice_b: 50 feet away from the bus
choice_c: Immediately across without stopping
choice_d: Approximately 10 feet away from the side of the bus to a position where the driver can see them
explanation: Students should walk approximately 10 feet away from the side of the school bus to a position where the driver can see them, then to a location at least 10 feet in front of the right corner of the bumper.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 10 - School Buses, p. 10-4

question: After unloading, how far should students walk away from the side of the bus?
choice_a: At least 100 feet
choice_b: They should stay right next to the bus
choice_c: There is no set distance as long as they face away from the bus
choice_d: At least 10 feet, to a position where the driver can plainly see all students
explanation: Tell students to exit the bus and walk at least 10 feet away from the side of the bus to a position where the driver can plainly see all students.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 10 - School Buses, p. 10-4

question: What should a driver check for during a post-trip inspection of the school bus?
choice_a: Only the mirror adjustment
choice_b: Only the fuel level
choice_c: Articles left on the bus and sleeping students
choice_d: Only tire tread depth
explanation: The post-trip inspection includes walking through and around the bus looking for articles left on the bus, sleeping students, open windows and doors, mechanical/operational problems, and damage or vandalism.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 10 - School Buses, p. 10-5

question: As a general rule, when is student safety and control best maintained during an emergency or impending crisis?
choice_a: By calling parents before making any decision
choice_b: By evacuating immediately in every situation
choice_c: By keeping students on the bus, if doing so does not expose them to unnecessary risk or injury
choice_d: By having students exit through windows regardless of the situation
explanation: As a general rule, student safety and control is best maintained by keeping students on the bus during an emergency, if doing so does not expose them to unnecessary risk or injury.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 10 - School Buses, p. 10-6

question: Which of these situations requires the driver to evacuate the bus?
choice_a: A student feels carsick
choice_b: The bus is on fire or there is a threat of fire, or is stalled on or adjacent to a railroad crossing
choice_c: The bus is running five minutes behind schedule
choice_d: The bus air conditioning stops working
explanation: The driver must evacuate the bus when it is on fire or there is a threat of fire, it is stalled on or adjacent to a railroad crossing, its position may change and increase danger, there is imminent danger of collision, or a hazardous materials spill requires quick evacuation.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 10 - School Buses, p. 10-6

question: How far off the road, in the direction of oncoming traffic, should a safe place be during a bus evacuation?
choice_a: At least 100 feet
choice_b: There is no minimum distance
choice_c: At least 500 feet
choice_d: At least 10 feet
explanation: A safe place will be at least 100 feet off the road in the direction of oncoming traffic, to keep students from being hit by debris if another vehicle collides with the bus.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 10 - School Buses, p. 10-6

question: If there is a risk from spilled hazardous materials, how far upwind should students be led during an evacuation?
choice_a: At least 20 feet
choice_b: At least 300 feet
choice_c: At least 50 feet
choice_d: There is no distance specified for hazmat spills
explanation: Lead students upwind of the bus at least 300 feet if there is a risk from spilled hazardous materials.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 10 - School Buses, p. 10-6

question: Before ordering an evacuation, how should the driver secure the bus?
choice_a: Only turn on the interior dome light
choice_b: Leave the transmission in Drive to allow quick repositioning
choice_c: Leave the engine running for lighting
choice_d: Place transmission in Park or Neutral, set parking brakes, shut off the engine, and remove the ignition key
explanation: To secure the bus before evacuation, the driver places the transmission in Park (or Neutral), sets the parking brakes, shuts off the engine, removes the ignition key, and activates hazard-warning lights.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 10 - School Buses, p. 10-7

question: What defines a "passive" railroad-highway crossing?
choice_a: A crossing only used by freight trains
choice_b: A crossing with flashing lights and gates
choice_c: A crossing that does not have any type of traffic control device
choice_d: A crossing marked with a stop sign and a police officer present
explanation: A passive crossing does not have any type of traffic control device; the decision to proceed rests entirely with the driver, who must search for trains and decide if there is sufficient clear space to cross safely.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 10 - School Buses, p. 10-7

question: What characterizes an "active" railroad-highway crossing?
choice_a: A crossing that never carries train traffic anymore
choice_b: A crossing only for use during daylight hours
choice_c: A crossing with no signage at all
choice_d: A traffic control device installed at the crossing, such as flashing red lights with or without bells and gates
explanation: Active crossings have a traffic control device installed to regulate traffic, including flashing red lights with or without bells, and flashing red lights with bells and gates.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 10 - School Buses, p. 10-7

question: If the gate at a railroad crossing stays down after the train has passed, what should the driver do?
choice_a: Back up and find an alternate route immediately without notifying anyone
choice_b: Carefully drive around the gate since the train has passed
choice_c: Not drive around the gate; call the dispatcher instead
choice_d: Honk the horn until the gate rises
explanation: If the gate stays down after the train passes, do not drive around the gate; instead, call your dispatcher.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 10 - School Buses, p. 10-8

question: How close and how far should a school bus stop from the nearest rail at a crossing?
choice_a: No closer than 15 feet and no farther than 50 feet
choice_b: There is no set distance, only 'a safe distance'
choice_c: No closer than 100 feet
choice_d: Exactly 5 feet
explanation: Stop no closer than 15 feet and no farther than 50 feet from the nearest rail, where you have the best view of the tracks.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 10 - School Buses, p. 10-8

question: At a multiple-track crossing, once you are sure no train is approaching on any track, what should you do?
choice_a: Stop again between each set of tracks
choice_b: Change to a higher gear halfway across for speed
choice_c: Proceed across all of the tracks until you have completely cleared them, without changing gears
choice_d: Wait for a police escort before proceeding
explanation: At a multiple-track crossing, stop only before the first set of tracks; once sure no train is approaching on any track, proceed across all tracks until completely cleared, crossing in a low gear without changing gears.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 10 - School Buses, p. 10-8

question: If a school bus stalls or is trapped on the tracks, what should the driver do?
choice_a: Attempt to push the bus off the tracks alone
choice_b: Get everyone out and off the tracks immediately, moving away at an angle both away from the tracks and toward the train
choice_c: Move everyone to the back of the bus for safety
choice_d: Stay on the bus and wait for help
explanation: If the bus stalls or is trapped on the tracks, get everyone out and off the tracks immediately, moving away from the bus at an angle that is both away from the tracks and toward the train.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 10 - School Buses, p. 10-9

question: As a general rule, how much should be added to the length of the school bus to determine an acceptable containment or storage area at a crossing?
choice_a: 5 feet
choice_b: 15 feet
choice_c: No addition is needed; use the bus length exactly
choice_d: 50 feet
explanation: As a general rule, add 15 feet to the length of the school bus to determine an acceptable amount of containment or storage area on the far side of a crossing.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 10 - School Buses, p. 10-8

question: If a serious behavior problem occurs while driving, what should the driver do?
choice_a: Turn around in the seat to address the student while still driving
choice_b: Radio the parents immediately while continuing to drive
choice_c: Stop the bus and park in a safe location off the road before addressing it
choice_d: Ignore it until the end of the route
explanation: To handle a serious problem, stop the bus, park in a safe location off the road, secure the bus (taking the ignition key if leaving your seat), and address the offender calmly but firmly.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 10 - School Buses, p. 10-9

question: Where is a driver permitted to put a student off the bus for a discipline issue?
choice_a: Nowhere; students may never be removed from the bus
choice_b: Only at school or at his or her designated school bus stop
choice_c: At any convenient location along the route
choice_d: At the nearest police station only
explanation: Never put a student off the bus except at school or at his or her designated school bus stop; if the offense is serious, call for a school administrator or the police.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 10 - School Buses, p. 10-9

question: Air-braked trucks, buses, trailers, and converter dollies built on or after what date are required to have antilock braking systems (ABS)?
choice_a: March 1, 1999
choice_b: March 1, 1998
choice_c: January 1, 2000
choice_d: January 1, 1995
explanation: The Department of Transportation requires antilock braking systems on air brake vehicles (trucks, buses, trailers, and converter dollies) built on or after March 1, 1998.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 10 - School Buses, p. 10-10

question: When braking hard in an emergency on a bus with ABS, what should the driver do?
choice_a: Pump the brakes rapidly for best control
choice_b: Shift into neutral before braking
choice_c: Do not pump the brakes
choice_d: Apply the parking brake instead of the service brake
explanation: In emergency braking, do not pump the brakes on a bus with ABS; brake as you always have, using only the force necessary to stop safely and stay in control.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 10 - School Buses, p. 10-9

question: Which of the following is true about what ABS does NOT do?
choice_a: ABS eliminates the need for regular brake maintenance
choice_b: ABS allows safe following distances to be reduced by half
choice_c: ABS won't necessarily shorten stopping distance and won't allow you to drive faster or follow more closely
choice_d: ABS guarantees a shorter stopping distance every time
explanation: ABS won't allow you to drive faster, follow more closely, or drive less carefully, and won't necessarily shorten stopping distance; it helps maintain vehicle control during hard braking.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 10 - School Buses, p. 10-10

question: What is the manual's guidance on backing a school bus?
choice_a: It is strongly discouraged and should never be done when students are outside the bus
choice_b: It is only allowed at the school, never on the route
choice_c: It requires a second driver in the vehicle at all times
choice_d: It should be done routinely at every stop to maximize visibility
explanation: Backing a school bus is strongly discouraged; you should back your bus only when you have no other safe way to move the vehicle, and never when students are outside of the bus.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 10 - School Buses, p. 10-10

question: How much tail swing can a school bus have?
choice_a: Up to three feet
choice_b: Up to one foot
choice_c: School buses have no tail swing
choice_d: Up to ten feet
explanation: A school bus can have up to a three-foot tail swing; drivers need to check mirrors before and during any turning movements to monitor it.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 10 - School Buses, p. 10-10

question: What does the manual say happens to a school bus in strong winds?
choice_a: Strong winds have no measurable effect on a bus
choice_b: The side of the bus acts like a sail and can push the bus sideways or even tip it over
choice_c: Wind primarily affects fuel economy, not handling
choice_d: Wind only affects the bus when it is empty
explanation: Strong winds affect the handling of the school bus; the side of a school bus acts like a sail on a sailboat, and strong winds can push it sideways, off the road, or even tip it over.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 10 - School Buses, p. 10-10
